chapters.title: The Song of Songs Begins
chapters.synopsis: The bride opens the song of songs, longing for her beloved and recalling how the daughters of Jerusalem admire him. Though sun-darkened from keeping the vineyards, she is comely, and the bridegroom answers her with words of tender praise.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: Bride and bridegroom exchange first words of love

chapters.title: The Rose of Sharon
chapters.synopsis: The bride calls herself the rose of Sharon and the lily of the valleys, and her beloved a banner of love over her. He calls her to rise up and come away, for the winter is past, the flowers appear on the earth, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in the land.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: Springtime invitation: rise up and come away

chapters.title: Seeking Him Whom She Loves
chapters.synopsis: By night the bride seeks him whom her soul loves, asking the watchmen of the city until she finds him and will not let him go. The chapter closes with the splendor of King Solomon's procession, crowned in the day of his espousals and the gladness of his heart.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: The bride's search; Solomon's wedding procession

chapters.title: A Garden Enclosed
chapters.synopsis: The bridegroom praises his bride from head to foot, declaring her altogether fair and without spot. He calls her a garden enclosed, a spring shut up, a fountain sealed, and she invites him to come into his garden and eat its pleasant fruits.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: The bridegroom's praise; the garden enclosed

chapters.title: The Beloved Sought and Praised
chapters.synopsis: The bride dreams that her beloved knocks by night, but when she rises he has withdrawn, and she seeks him sorrowing through the city. Charged by the daughters of Jerusalem, she describes him as the chiefest among ten thousand, altogether lovely.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: The beloved missed by night, then described

chapters.title: Fair as the Moon
chapters.synopsis: The daughters of Jerusalem ask where the beloved has gone, and the bride answers that he feeds among the lilies in his garden. He in turn praises her as beautiful as Tirzah, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, the choice one of her mother.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: Mutual belonging; fair as the moon

chapters.title: How Fair Is Love
chapters.synopsis: The bridegroom continues his praise of the bride's grace and beauty, delighting in her as in the fruitful vine and the palm tree. She answers that she is her beloved's and his desire is toward her, and invites him out to the villages and vineyards.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: Delight in the bride; I am my beloved's

chapters.title: Love Strong as Death
chapters.synopsis: The bride asks to be set as a seal upon her beloved's heart, for love is strong as death and many waters cannot quench it. The song closes with care for a little sister, the worth of a vineyard beyond price, and a final call for the beloved to make haste.

segments.speaker: solomon
segments.note: A seal upon the heart; love unquenchable
